consumer: The engine's reload-eligibility logic (item::reload_option / gun reload-ammo enumeration) asking 'does the wielded gun have exactly one unambiguous compatible ammo so no selection menu is raised?'
scope: The full reload-ammo search the engine considers (compatible ammo across inventory, worn, and reachable map/vehicle sources), reduced to a single-vs-multiple-option verdict — not just on-person carried items
decisive_source: src/arcopolis_export.cpp::write_carried_items, which only dumps raw wielded/worn/inventory item records (type_id, charges, count_by_charges) and computes no ammo-compatibility or option-count predicate
divergence: Avatar wields a gun while carrying two different compatible ammo types (or one compatible ammo on-person plus another in an adjacent container/vehicle): the engine would raise a selection menu (>1 option), but the carried_items dump exposes only raw items and lets the frontend re-derive 'single ammo' from a partial on-person view, wrongly concluding the reload is unambiguous
